surface_features: title contains explicit emotional words or personal identifiers (e.g., 'I hate', first-person self-reference, identity statements)
constructs.theoretical_construct: emotional/personal framing of the post title

features.name: title_emotional_or_personal_identifier
features.definition: Does the post title contain an explicit emotional expression or explicit personal identifier (e.g., first-person self-reference or stated personal identity/experience)?
features.spec: Read only the title. Return 1 if the title explicitly contains (a) emotion words/expressions (e.g., hate, love, angry, afraid, annoyed, feel) or (b) explicit personal identifiers: first-person self-reference (I, me, my, I'm) or a stated personal identity, role or experience of the author (e.g., 'as a woman', 'I'm a veteran'). Return 0 otherwise. Ignore the 'CMV:' prefix. Judge only the title's literal wording; do not infer from the argument. Do not treat any view-change/delta announcement as evidence. Empty or missing title gives null.

h0: title_emotional_or_personal_identifier has no association with the probability of delta (coefficient = 0).
h1: Posts with title_emotional_or_personal_identifier = 1 have lower probability of OP view change than those with 0 (coefficient < 0).
note: 'Emotional or personal identifiers' is ambiguous; operationalized as explicit emotion words or first-person/personal identity references in the title, combined as OR. Binary presence only; no intensity scale. OLS on binary delta is a linear probability model; association only. Title text is current supplied text; timing unknown, though titles rarely contain outcome announcements.
